column9: Notes/Outlook (Updated 7/10/2026)
It's only Year 3 of Wemby and he's already reached the Finals and was an MVP finalist. Unreal talent and the obvious 1.01 for a long time to come.
More of the same from SGA as the two-time MVP. We know what to expect out of an elite performer and a unanimous top 2-3 dynasty pick in all formats.
Luka has continued to dominate in the fantasy department. He's beginning to enter his prime with LeBron out the door.
Jokic is still dominating at a high level. He's 31 now but his game will age like fine wine. Averaging anything close to a triple double is par for the course at this point.
Flagg has looked as advertised despite some normal rookie struggles and he'll keep getting better quickly. Expect him to remain a consensus top 5-10 player.
Cade Cunningham was awesome this past year and stayed firmly in the mix in the MVP race. Arguably the best guard in the East.
Tatum should be back to 100% coming into this season. Expect massive numbers with Jaylen Brown gone.
Ant gets himself a co-star with LaMelo Ball to run things with. Expect more of the same moving forward.
Jalen Johnson came into his own this year as a fantasy performer. He remains the main man for Atlanta.
Maxey has been stepping up as an elite fantasy player, but with the addition of Jaylen Brown and pending Joel Embiid's health, this will eat into his touches a bit.
Don't overthink this one. Boozer is a blue chip talent and a clear top 10-15 dynasty asset from Day 1.
Scottie Barnes has been fantastic for Toronto this year and continues posting a steady, well-rounded fantasy game. Him and Kawhi should mesh real well.
I'm fully expecting to push Haliburton back into the top 10 this next season, just as I have with Tatum. We'll see when he's healthy. We know the ceiling when he's rolling.
Sengun was pretty disappointing in the playoffs. Lots of upside here, especially in the fantasy department. His value feels a bit fluid moving forward.
For some, Dybantsa will be their 1.01. He's a real star talent, but there are questions needing answered in the fantasy department.
Very little change here for Giannis as he heads over to the 305. He remains the clearcut best player for Miami and will continue delivering elite numbers.
Peterson goes where we expected in Utah, where he will commend a clear starting role from Day 1. Will the playmaking return to his HS levels?
Frankly, I've been a little disappointed by Amen Thompson relative to the expectations coming in. Still an elite player and asset to hold onto, though.
I still believe in Evan Mobley and have hope for more here. This is a crucial year to show it if LeBron comes home for one last hurrah.
Harper has already been flashing plenty of star potential so far. He and Castle are the future alongside Wemby. He may need a little longer to be fully unleashed.
JDub underwhelmed this year compared to last year's big jump, only playing 33 games and never looking 100%. I'm buying if he's valued for less than top 25 prices.
Kon is the big benefactor of LaMelo Ball's departure. Expect the numbers to go up and the on-ball reps to send him to the moon.
Paolo has still yet to flash a more fantasy-friendly game for categories. This is a crucial year for him and Orlando to make a splash.
I'm still not the biggest fan of the Giddler, but I can't deny that he's been great for fantasy and this all feels sustainable.
An ECF sweep will prompt normal doom and gloom, but Spida is approaching 30 and there are questions if he's on the decline soon. He got a massive payday from CLE.
Deni and Portland are in a weird spot right now with the addition of Ja Morant, but I imagine Deni will remain in about the same spot.
Chet has taken plenty of heat after the Thunder's WCF loss. I'm still expecting him to be a perennial All-Defense guy for a long time if he stays healthy.
More of the same from Franz Wagner, a continually good player with some team fit concerns and how him and Paolo mesh.
Unsurprisingly, Austin Reaves stays put in LA with a big contract in hand. Expect him to continue crushing and staying high in my ranks through his prime.
Caleb Wilson is my current 1.04 and has a lot of juice to his fantasy game. Will need time to develop more on offense but has a ton of potential here in CHI.
Murray was great this past year as Denver's healthiest player on the roster. Expecting another strong year from him with DEN not likely to make many moves.
Since being traded to the Clippers, Garland is starting to return to being the All-Star we've seen when healthy. Very excited about him leading LAC moving forward.
Congratulations to Jalen Brunson and the New York Knicks. He's still well within his prime but we will continue to monitor things as he turns 30 this next season.
LaMelo joins Anthony Edwards in Minnesota to form one of the most fiery backcourts in the NBA. Don't think this changes a ton for LaMelo.
Jalen Duren is currently looking at sign-and-trade scenarios out of Detroit. I don't see any big jumps in his value. Staying the same or dropping a little are my best guesses.
We know what to expect with Booker, but he's almost 30 and remains in the same Suns situation. Is a drop coming soon?
KAT was a crucial piece for the Knicks in winning a championship. After a lot of questions about trades, he feels secure on this roster moving forward.
Murphy is on the trade block with a lot of suitors. I'd imagine most landing spots will keep his value fairly insulated, but I'm guessing he stays put in NOLA.
This Jaylen Brown trade is going to shake up both Boston and Philly. What will his role look like as the potential third guy behind Maxey and Embiid?
Trae Young can likely maintain fantasy value on some level, but I'm a bit concerned about the short-term splits for this Wizards squad with Dybantsa and AD.
Castle has continued to make strong progress in his second year with San Antonio. What does the ceiling look like with Dylan Harper and De'Aaron Fox in the mix?
Kon and Miller got handed the keys with LaMelo's departure. I've always been a bit skeptical of Miller, but this is his chance to show he can reach stardm.
Bam sticks around in Miami and will be their second best player next to Giannis. They'll have a lot on their shoulders this year pending more FA moves.
One big short-term loser of the Jaylen Brown trade: their young phenom VJ Edgecombe. Still in on him long-term, though.
I'm not terribly worried about Lauri moving forward, either leaving via trade or with JJJ and Kessler in the frontcourt. Dude's just a good player.
Despite some playoff struggles, Clingan had an amazing year and has taken a big leap developmentally. How much further can he go?
Walker Kessler lands in a very favorable situation in Los Angeles as the clearcut starter. Him, Luka and Reaves will make for a fun trio.
Sarr's outlook is not looking as good as it was early in the season with AD, Trae Young and the 1st overall pick coming in.
George has established he belongs as a longer term starter. in Utah. What does Darryn Peterson incoming mean for him?
Acuff has been a straight-up star for Arkansas and there's no telling just how much further he can keep going. Concerns are obvious and there is a chance he's a bust.
Edey is a dominant fantasy player when healthy, but his health has been a concern so far. Monitoring this, but comfortable with him in the top 50.
Brandon Ingram takes a massive jump back to the top 50 in LAC. Tons of freedom and usage to soak up with Darius Garland as his PG. He's back to his NOLA days.
JJJ got traded to Utah in a deal that feels like it happened forever ago. He will be a core starter in a MASSIVE starting 5.
Wagler was incredible for Illinois. He has some concern areas and needs to put on more weight, but the higher-level outcomes in LAC are very exciting.
I have a lot of questions about Sabonis moving forward at age 30 and in a shaky Kings setting. Great fantasy player still.
Okongwu continues to grow his game further as he expands his game from 3. Currently 37.9% from deep on 5.2 attempts.
Bane has remained at a high level even in Orlando. He's been their mainstay all year with plenty of injuries up and down the roster.
KD and the Rockets have had some real turmoil this season, but it seems to have cooled out. How many more years does he have left at this level?
James Harden was... well, he was James Harden again, as expected. He'll presumably sign a multi-year deal to stick around in Cleveland.
Mikel Brown has the makings of another star fantasy guard. He's not without his concerns but the upside is very strong.
Fox was frankly awful during the playoffs for the Spurs. Castle and Harper ran circles around him. His days are very numbered.
It wasn't noticed as much this past year with how bad NOLA is, but Zion quietly had another strong season. Injuries remain a concern.
Steph Curry is still Steph Curry even at age 38, but there have been a lot of times he's looked human recently. Hold and enjoy the rest of the ride.
AD gets traded to Washington as they aim to speed up the rebuild. Curious how he and Sarr mesh.
CMB has looked like a fantasy star in the making and was excellent for the Raptors in the playoffs. Super excited for his development.
Kel'el Ware is obviously talented, but the motor has been a real concern from college to now. He joins a wide-open Bucks team and has a chance to break out.
Zubac is now locked into the Pacers as a starter. I have questions about the fit but we know the talent and fantasy game is rock-solid.
He's baaaaack. Kawhi returns to Toronto for another run at a championship on a very interesting Raptors team. Health (and the Aspiration scandal) remain a concern.
Flemings ends up in a very favorable situation with Atlanta. He could easily work his way up to a long-term starting role.
Kyrie is coming back to Dallas with a great situation for him and Cooper Flagg. Injuries and missed time remain a concern.
To me, Siakam is one of the more underrated top-end dynasty players and he feels very undervalued relative to the production. Still, he is now 32.
There will be some concern about Caleb Wilson in town, but I'm not worried much about Buzelis. He, Giddey and Wilson are the long-term future and should mesh well.
We know what to expect with OG Anunoby at this point. He's clearly made his mark on the Knicks and is such a winning connective piece.
Derrick White has been incredible this year. It's amazing how good he's been for fantasy despite the uncharacteristic sub-40 FG%.
Despite going back home to Milwaukee, Herro ends up in a bit of a messy guard room. Not sure what to expect from him.
Missed time remains a massive concern from Joel Embiid. He's only played 96 of 246 possible regular season games in the last three seasons.
This MEM-POR trade is fascinating. If Ja really wants to turn things around, this is his chance, but he comes into a very weird lineup (Scoot, Dame, Jrue).
Dyson Daniels remains an all-world defender for Atlanta, but he took a slight step back from last year's breakout candidate.
Ausar Thompson has been an otherworldly defender in the playoffs. Is there hope the offensive breakout comes this year?
Suggs needs to stay healthy for Orlando to be at their best. Very impactful player on the whole.
As expected, Coward has been up and down, but the highs have been very exciting. I remain high on him moving forward.
Rollins has had an awesome breakout year in MIL. There's a lot of guards here now, but he is very clearly the most talented.
NAW rightfully won Most Improved Player this year and risen into such a high-level player under Quin Synder.
Jarrett Allen continues to be Jarrett Allen. He's always younger than you'd think. Could he be a trade target with the market on bigs staying hot?
George might see a slight squeeze on opportunities with Dybantsa here, but he has a lot of good malleability as a role player. I'm keeping him high.
Queen flashed very high potential so far in his rookie season. The defense remains a major concern, but I'm still bought in on some level.
McDaniels continues to flash fantasy upside as he gets better in this career year he's having. Great two-way player and is building up a reputation as an iron man.
We've seen some good stuff out of Sheppard that remind us why he went so high in drafts, but the concerns are still there, especially on defense.
Pritchard is primed for the breakout with Jaylen Brown gone. How far can he scale up with more freedom than ever before in Joe Mazzulla's offense?
Ace Bailey is one of the losers of Utah adding Darryn Peterson. He'll likely play the 6th man role this year if Walker Kessler sticks around.
Hartenstein ends up staying in OKC on a more cap-friendly deal. Him, Mara and Sorber make for an intriguing big man rotation.
MPJ takes a hit in the short term with Julius Randle now in town. Watching them play basketball on the same side of the court will be... interesting?
Coby White returns to Charlotte with a big contract in hand and a starting job with LaMelo gone. Are we going to see a possible return to his Chicago peak?
Scoot missed a lot of the season. He's had some hit-or-miss performances but he really turned it on in the playoffs. Lot of questions about POR's guards.
Burries has played himself firmly into lottery status and possesses a lot of the winning, two-way traits you want to see in a long-term NBA starter.
As always, Quickley is streaky and can run hot or cold depending on the night, but he's locked into TOR for the long haul and playing well.
Dubious Handle goes back to the Big Apple. He and Michael Porter Jr. are going to chuck up plenty of tour dates this year.
Mikal Bridges took a step back this year despite the Knicks winning the championship. We'll see how he bounces back.
If you're looking for a ready-to-go rookie with a juicy fantasy profile and tons of skills that NBA teams look for in role players, Yaxel is your man.
Claxton has trended down towards the end of the Nets years, but he's in a great place to return to form in Chicago with a clearcut role.
Aday Mara has a lot of high-end fantasy upside, but managers are going to need to be patient to see it emerge.
Love Morez Johnson's potential fantasy game. There's a lot of pathways to becoming an elite asset for years to come. Ceiling is much higher than you think.
Jalen Green had a really rough first season with the Suns with all the missed time with his hamstring. Hopefully he builds momentum going into next season.
Watson is a solid all-around player who could be a long-term staple for Denver. He's taken a huge leap over the last few months.
Naz Reid is due for a potential breakout with LaMelo Ball gone and looking like a look for a starting job.
I've raised Murray a decent bit up here as he's coming back and looking OK following the Achilles tear. I'm skeptical still about his long-term outlook but deserves the bump.
Tari Eason lost tens of millions of dollars this past year, but on a relatively cheap deal, he's due for a solid year.
Ajay has been incredible this year and in the playoffs. Unreal find by OKC. The leap next year could be special.
The Magic need Anthony Black to be more consistent and closer to his strong stretch of play this past season.
I think we know by now that LaVine is not super conducive to winning as a leading scorer, but the stats are stats all the same in a fantasy setting.
Fears has, unsurprisingly, not been all that good or conducive to winning. The advanced numbers are bad. This is pretty normal for guards. I'm staying the course.
I am not one who tends to overreact to Summer League, but Egor has been extremely good. Sophomore year jump incoming.
Miles Bridges is the new starting PF for Phoenix and gives them a clearer piece to rely on in the frontcourt.
Not that it ever felt super likely he'd leave, but Mark Williams does return to Phoenix on a pretty team-friendly deal.
I've been low on Keegan Murray for years. I just don't know that I buy him being much more than this. Clean stat profile, but nothing too exciting.
Hart has shot well from 3 this year and continues to deliver on the do-everything role he's made his bread off of.
Despite a career-PPG year, Nembhard didnt step up like we hoped he would. A step back is likely coming when Haliburton is back to form.
We need to be patient and see what happens with Tre Johnson, but he will take one of the biggest hits from everything Washington has done since the trade deadline.
Okorie was a star for Stanford this year. Is he the star Cade Cunningham has always needed next to him? Time will tell, but there are star signs here.
Joan is rising in a big way this offseason. He gets a big time vote of confidence from Minnesota as the center of the future when Rudy Gobert's time is up.
Vassell has really struggled recently compared to these last few years. Still has plenty of potential to tap into, but he may be expendable soon.
RJ Barrett stays behind in Toronto and will likely remain a starter. His scoring will likely take a dip.
Malauch was always going to require patience. If you have him, you need to understand what you signed up for. Some flashes have been interesting so far.
Day'Ron Sharpe takes a big jump as the incumbent starting center. Personally, I feel that the contract (2yr/$20m) screams sell-high with such a lack of commitment.
Hannes is the best rebounder in the class, bar none. The athleticism and lack of defense remains a concern but the measurements at the Combine are a big positive.
I've been a bit lower on PG13 for a while now, but with landing in Boston, he's taking a big step.
I'm expecting a good year out of Camara with Portland lacking in their forward depth. Good role player who can do a bit of everything.
Norman Powell has been on a heater this past year for Miami in their tinkered offense. He signs with Chicago where he'll continue to have a good green light.
Turner has been pretty disappointing this year for Milwaukee. Will be interesting what the plan is with him if Giannis is traded.
It feels like Cason Wallace's fantasy upside is limited, but I still like him enough long-term with his elite defense, especially if he goes elsewhere.
PJ Washington ends up in an interesting situation with Lively hurt, Gafford on the block and having an interesting fit with Morez Johnson.
Jabari's career to date has been really disappointing. He's been a good role player with a lot of inconsistency.
Poeltl's back may be cooked. Wondering if he ends up getting salary dumped but there is still hope for him.
With FVV, expect him to return to form on some level post-ACL tear. He'll be crucial to Houston's success this year.
I've been underwhelmed by Sharpe, who just doesn't possess much of a fantasy game besides scoring and hasn't played all that well relative to his high usage.
I'm not making much of the 15-game sample from last year, but in a starting/key 6th man role, I'm hopeful in seeing Jerome have a nice year.
More of the same as usual for Rudy Gobert, who delivers on his normal. LaMelo's playmaking will help him.
Kristaps Porzingis continues to suffer from POTS and may miss time here and there. Very solid fantasy performer when he does play.
Stirtz has some question marks, but the fantasy appeal should come with zero questions. Great shooter and is an iron man.
I still like Aldama, but it's hard to really know what MEM looks like at their best. I think he's a key rotation piece, but Boozer, Lopez and Stewart hurt his value.
Gordon has missed some time at different points of this year. With everyone on the table, will someone try and trade for him?
Queta looked like a very solid starter for Boston this past year. Despite landing a big payday, he and Mitchell Robinson will split time.
McCain loses some value on the whole after going to OKC, but he's been playing extremely well with the opportunities given to him so far.
I have a lot of questions about Swain and how his game translates to the NBA in a new role, but the appeal as a do-everything wing/forward is all there.
Carr is in a great situation to play a good role as a rookie. He should've never fallen to the mid-20s in real life.
John Collins heads to Detroit to replace Tobias Harris. Frankly, it's a bit of a step-down for Detroit, but it is a lateral move for Collins' fantasy value.
Jaquez's strong 6MOY campaign ends with him a bit buried in Milwaukee. Expecting he gets moved if he doesn't take up a big role.
I think Bilal is done as far as any higher level outcomes, but he's had a good season and has some good role player outcomes here. Still very young.
This next season is a make-or-break one for me with Lively. I'm largely out on him being a top 100 player again if the foot injuries continue.
I'm not sure Holland's true potential will ever be realized in Detroit. He's just not able to contribute much yet.
Raynaud has been excelling so far in Sacramento. Despite questions around the center position, he should remain a core piece.
I'm fully expecting LeBron's final year to be 2026-2027, and by default, his value is pretty much deflated from here. We'll see where he ends up.
Anderson is a great shooter and playmaker who offers a lot of solid skills from a fantasy perspective. What does his role look like without LaMelo?
I'm still willing to be patient with Thomas Sorber even though OKC's center depth looks weird right now. Very fantasy-friendly profile.
Carter Bryant is a bit of a mystery box in terms of upside. The fantasy game is meh so far but the upside and phyiscal tools are very intriguing.
Grown folks online tried saying Ayo is a bottom 10 role player in the NBA. Minnesota dropped a bag on him this offseason.
I've been a longtime Marshall truther and he's been surging recently. One of the more undervalued win-now fantasy targets out there.
Dame Time returns this fall, but how much do we get coming off the achilles tear and the heavy guard rotation (Morant, Henderson, Holiday)?
Andrew Wiggins comes back to Miami on a more team-friendly deal. They'll need a lot of him with Miami's depleted depth post-Giannis.
I'm still in on Christian Braun being a good player in his career despite Peyton Watson running away as the better player.
Philon is going to require some serious patience. He's currently the fourth guard in the pecking order for Philadelphia.
There's a lot of red flags in Nate Ament's profile, especially for categories leagues, but he should get plenty of run in Milwaukee.
Podz had a career-high in scoring this year, but it feels like he's never going to get much respect online. Still a decent player.
Tyson has evolved into a clear foundational piece for Cleveland. Not sure what the ceiling is but the highs this past year have been solid.
Name value and the Lakers tax on Grimes is going to lead to him being overvalued. Fine player but got paid too much in free agency.
Will Riley has had some ridiculous stretches of play for Washington. AJ Dybantsa hurts him short term. It's on him to improve this year to stick.
KPJ returns to Milwaukee on a player option with a very muddled backcourt. He'll likely still get minutes.
Unsurprisingly, Ayton has looked better than expected because of Luka and Reaves. Numbers are typical but I don't see more long-term upside.
I expected Gafford to get traded, but with Lively's status continually up in the air, we'll see what happens.
As expected, Charlotte got some frontcourt help behind Moussa with Hannes Steinbach aned Nas Reid, but I think he should remain a steady piece.
Nesmith only played about half the season with Indiana's tanking antics. He'll be back to his normal defined 3&D role this season.
Kasparas ends up in a situation where he can commend more minutes in a rebuild. Still hopeful he can pan out despite the short term logjam in the backcourt.
Gillespie has been excellent this year for Phoenix. I expect him to get a nice payday to stay with the Suns this summer.
Champagnie has had a much more impactful season/playoffs than the counting stats might tell you. Is there more coming for him?
One of the more consistently undervalued big men, WCJ had a bit of a resurgence after a bad 2024-2025 season. He and Vuc will split time.
I think we've figured out who Jonathan Kuminga is by now and isn't going to hit those high upside marks we hoped for. Fascinated to see where he signs.
Kyle Filipowski finds himself in a good position to continue maintaining a solid role with Utah. This could be a key year for him.
Stewart ends up going to a pretty favorable situation in Memphis as the backup big to Zach Edey. I think he'll be more fantasy relevant than people might expect.
Brooks had an electric year with Phoenix and scoring 20+ PPG for the first time. I don't expect this to continue but he should continue playing a steady role.
Miami gutting their depth chart definitely helps Davion Mitchell's case, but I don't expect him to keep a firm starting job after free agency.
Jimmy Butler suffered a devastating ACL tear this January. He's a psycho and will aim to return soon, but will he ever be the same player again at age 37?
The wheels have started to fall off for Cam in Denver. We'll see if he can bounce back this year (preferably if Peyton Watson is gone).
CJ's still got it. He's in for probably one more year with Atlanta with a high-scoring role.
This offseason has given us numerous signs that Hugo is a very valuable player that Boston really believes in. Is the sophomore breakout coming?
Karim Lopez is going to be a work in progress, but if he hits, he's going to be a solid player that NBA teams will pay a lot of money for.
Tarris Reed and JQ make the backup big spot a little weird, but Reed is a different flavor with some muscle that should work great with Wemby.
Graves is a statistical darling with a lot to like about his player. I have a lot of questions about his long term upside.
One of the more underdiscussed Warriors storylines is that Santos has found his way into the rotation and had some good looks. Interesting hold going into next season.
Essengue is far from a complete product and has a lot to work on still after missing his entire rookie year. He'll have to work his way into a reserve role.
Allen had his best year and popped off for Phoenix with their need for scorers. He'll play a bench role for Charlotte and hope to keep it up.
Monk had a down year after starting to get phased out of Sacramento. I have to believe someone legitimately wants to trade for him.
Despite years of trade rumors, Herb is still in New Orleans and will continue anchoring their entire defense.
Remember Max Christie's hot run early into his Dallas tenure? Still remains a good player but he's not going much further than this.
Rui Hachimura didn't have to go far to his next team. He stays in town in LA and will have a similar enough role for the Clippers with less pressure than his Lakers gig.
We know who Green is at this point. He'll stick around in GSW until the wheels fall off. His fantasy game isn't what it used to be but he's still a great and valuable player.
Mathurin remains unsigned to date, and the Clippers-Aspiration investigation might hold them up longer.
I realize that this is a massive jump for BBall Paul, but the way he's played in these playoffs should guarantee him a multi-year offer and a more clearcut role.
Simons has fallen out of favor in the NBA and will settle for a bench role in a stacked Philly squad.
I've really liked what I've seen of Nique in his best moments this season in Sacramento. Hoping to see more this next year as he remains a key piece.
Wolf has a very appealing fantasy game, but he's not a good player at the NBA level yet and has a ways to go. Still definitely worth an investment in dynasty.
Mitchell Robinson finds a new home in Boston. Injuries remain a concern for him but him and Neemias Queta should maintain solid roles.
Jenkins looks to be a long-term staple for Detroit moving forward. He and Ebuka Okorie will be the main guards off the bench.
Cam Spencer is a testament to how stacked Memphis is with good-not-great guards. Who emerges of this group?
Jrue Holiday showed us that he's still got it this past year. With the Blazers' guard spots looking weird, what we can we expect for him?
Shead has been a solid NBA player to date and really proven me wrong. He's going to be in the NBA for a long time.
I'm a big Bruce Thornton fan. I think this fit is fantastic and could really allow him to shine. Could be a major steal in a few years.
All signs point to DeMar heading back to Toronto, staying close to home in LA or going to Miami.
Pippen is one of the forgotten guards of this group who has flashed really strong play at times (especially in the playoffs).
It'd be a surprise if Jordan Poole was done as an NBA player yet, but he was downright awful this year and got a lot of DNPs.
Minott has looked solid when getting the looks in Boston and moves onto Brooklyn in a clearer role. We'll see if that sustains this coming season.
After a one-year wonder performance in Atlanta/Cleveland, Hunter was dumped to Sacramento where he'll expect to take up a decent-sized role.
Aaron Wiggins is one of OKC's consolidation victims and heads to Atlanta to keep up in a solid role.
With the addition of Bennett Stirtz, this largely kills the Topic hype. I'm guessing he needs a trade to make it happen at this point.
Despite his size, Tre Jones has showed he belongs in the NBA still and can sustain a decent backup role in Chicago.
Despite Walker Kessler going down, Nurkic has been playing with a little gas left in the tank. Not expecting much after this season.
Hope to see Clayton have a mini sophomore breakout in Memphis. He'll definitely shoot better this next season. He's been dealt a weird hand so far.
Portis has dropped off the map a little this year and it remains to be seen if he'll tick back up into a more normal role for him.
Sam Hauser doesn't have much true upside, but he is a good 3&D player and can pop off for 9 3s now and again. He's an important cheap piece for Boston.
Saddiq Bey was scoring like crazy this year with 17.7 per game. This is pretty obviously not going to stay at this level.
Mamu got a big time payday to head to the Lakers where he'll face a ton of pressure as the presumed starting power forward.
The shooting is still far from ever being close to average, but the playmaking, pace and feel are pretty good for a young guard. How will he, George and Clayton mesh?
Timelord gets a nice 4-year deal to remain the backup center to Donovan Clingan. He was really good when healthy this year, as per usual.
Detroit is really going to feel the loss of Tobias Harris. I like the addition for the Spurs and expect him to continue playing a decent role.
Vucevic's value has continued to fall since leaving Chicago. He heads back home to Orlando where he'll play a bench role.
Traore has had some flashes of being a potentially good player in Brooklyn. Will likely play a good bench role this next season behind Mikel and Egor.
Sergio has a ton to like as a 6'6 point guard with good craftiness, passing and shooting. Dusty May will really like and try to weaponize his size.
Zuby will get some run with Atlanta. I have questions about the fit but they've needed more energy and size at the center position for some time now.
The Clippers should be jumping for joy with the scam contract they gave Kobe Sanders. Fully expecting him to outplay it and impact LAC in a big way.
Melton returns to Golden State on a team-friendly deal. He'll continue playing a rotation role with a good fantasy game.
Grant was one of the pieces traded in the Ja Morant deal. He's making absurd money and will get some minutes.
Wells is a better real-life player than fantasy as a 3&D wing. He'll keep playing good minutes for Memphis.
If/when Giannis is traded, Dieng could have a chance to be MIL's next big breakout star after Ryan Rollins for the rebuild. Keep an eye on him this summer.
TSJ has taken a step up when called upon in the playoffs and he should be looking at a better role this year, if Chris Finch stops being such a stickler.
Merrill is one of the very best shooters in the entire world. The upside isn't high but Sammy Buckets will get you, well, buckets.
Risacher's value is crashing hard right now and it remains to be seen if/how he can get it back.
Peat is very much a mystery box player with loads of athleticism. He'll need help getting fit into a role. Could be a solid defender at the NBA level.
With a 4-year guaranteed deal in hand, Thomas has a chance to be a core piece for Cleveland with some more fine-tuning.
Kalkbrenner went from looking at a starting job to being the potential 4th best big on this Hornets squad. He needs a trade to make it happen.
Not much more upside for the Magic to extract from Da Silva, but as a rotation player, I think he's good and should have a lengthy career in the NBA.
If you draft Cenac, proceed with caution in knowing he is a development project. He will need time to make it happen in Boston, but the ceiling could be very high.
Just as he's walking away with his 6MOY award, Keldon suddenly feels like an odd man out with San Antonio's recent string of moves, plus Carter Bryant rising.
Cardwell has flashed some really interesting play for Sacramento as an old-school rim protecting big. Great innings eater/backup to Sabonis and Raynaud.
LAC has not addressed the current big man situation at all through the draft or free agency as of yet. This is a great sign of their confidence in YKN.
We know what Oubre is and what his game looks like. He's a bucket but doesn't offer a ton of strong fantasy appeal besides that.
Once again, we've seen some flashes from Brice Sensabaugh, but with Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey in town, I think he needs a new team to make it happen.
Hendricks struggled to make it happen in Utah, but there are signs of life in Memphis. Keeping an eye here.
Ryan Nembhard finding a role as an UDFA was one of the bright spots of Dallas's season. Can he secure a solid long term contract this year?
Some people are going to be annoyed about this placement. I just don't know what to say about GG. Can score but not much else. Only gets run when MEM is bad.
Fleming will remain in a reserve role following the Suns' trade for Miles Bridges. Still hopeful he can pan out as him and Koa Peat fight for PF minutes.
Lu Dort remains in OKC as one of their core defenders. Will he stay here much longer?
I normally try and give some grace to young guards, but I'm pretty concerned with how things went in MIN and the fantasy game being pretty poor in CHI.
Jefferson will fit right in with this Brooklyn Nets identity built around passing at all positions. Good fantasy profile.
There is zero question that JQ looks like an elite athlete and defender from Day 1 in the NBA, but the offensive development is the big swing.
Isaiah Evans doesn't have a strong fantasy game, but the hope is the shooting is something to build on.
I don't care that Richie Saunders is almost 25 years old. Dude is a demon and has a real route to being a successful NBA player that outplays his draft position.
Deuce McBride scored more points than I anticipated this past year despite only playing half the season. I don't expect 12 PPG to remain the norm.
Awful news as we find out Donte DiVincenzo tore his achilles during the playoffs. We won't see him at all next year.
There's some real upside with Post here. Memphis made an interesting move to steal him away from Memphis as their third big.
Yang was completely unplayable as a rookie. Never thought much of him, but given the profile and the capital spent on him, you have to hold or buy low.
Larsson will need to step up for Miami with a lot of missing depth. Spo trusts him and he can play different roles as a glue guy.
Finally, pure mid. We know who Kyle Kuzma is and that he's a bad fantasy player. Don't much expect here in Milwaukee post-Giannis.
Scheierman took a step forward this year for Boston. With Jaylen Brown gone, expect him and Hugo Gonzalez to pick up some slack.
Strus barely played in 2025-2026 (12 GP). Expect him to remain in a decent role and keep hitting 3s.
Beal could be an interesting bargain bin player to stash if you're a contender and think he can come back to some form next year.
Moody was really coming up strong before a brutal patellar tendon tear. He has a lenthy road to recovery.
Clowney has gross percentages, but he's certainly improved overall this year. I don't think he's ever going to be a good NBA player, frankly.
The talent is still there for Jase Richardson, but the opportunities haven't been and his height and role are at odds. Hoping their next head coach sees the vision.
I couldn't think of a worse fit for Collin Sexton if I tried. He'll get some mileage with the Lakers but I'm not confident he looks all that good.
Royce heads to Charlotte after a career-high year in points. Expect him to play like his usual self we've seen at Utah, Brooklyn and Phoenix.
Karaban has some connective pieces to his game that should give him some fantasy appeal. Good leader and jack-of-all-trades.
Huff was not efficient this year, but there's a lot to like as a 3-point shooting center who racks up blocks. Hoping he returns to form in a backup role behind Zubac.
These Champagnie twin are good, man.  Really impressed by Justin's hard work in securing a full-time NBA role. High-percentile rebounder for his position.
We know what it is with Jalen Smith. He'll likely back up Nic Claxton at the 5 and should continue playing a decent role in Chicago.
Conwell has a pro-ready game built to help the Heat's bench from the jump. Expect him to start climbing in your drafts.
Ighodaro was impactful this year for Phoenix. Curious how things shake out with Maluach improving, Miles Bridges coming in, and Rasheer Fleming and Koa Peat.
Henri Veesaar forced his way into a long fall down draft boards to secure a guaranteed deal with the Hawks. He remains a priority 30s target.
Baba Miller got a big ol' payday with the Clippers on a 4-year deal. This is super notable and could be a great sign of what's to come.
Schroder has bounced around for a while. He's still got legs in the NBA depending on what Cleveland does with him.
I'm closely watching Asa Newell after some fiery games when he gets real minutes. Holding and buying if I can.
I love what I've seen from Penda so far and I'm high on him potentially earning a consistent role in 2026-2027.
Grand Theft Alvrado has been a solid contributor with the Knicks. He signed a team-friendly deal to stick around the champions.
Small's fantasy game has continued to pop when he plays for Memphis. Could be a real sleeper hit for deeper leagues here.
Kennard is playing a 3-point specialist role for the Lakers. I expect him to pick up some slack until Luka and Reaves are back.
Bona played a similar low-minute role again for the 76ers. Still a nice long-term bench piece to look at, but Andre Drummond is still good for the backup role.
This next year might be a make-or-break one for Salaun as Charlotte gears up with more frontcourt pieces in this upcoming draft.
This is quite a jump for Markovic, but after a great year of improvement that won him the ABA MVP and a nice-sized 4 year contract, he's absolutely a priority pickup.
I didn't respect Ja'Kobe Walter enough this past year. Curious how much further he's going into this next year.
Not much upside for Dunn at this point in his career, but I expect him to play a key role in LAC either starting next to Darius Garland or coming off the bench.
Walsh is still young and needs time, but upside is still there in his physical tools and the advanced numbers this season. Curious if he can carve out more in Year 3.
We barely saw Obi Toppin this year (24 games played). We'll hope to see him keep things back to '24-'25 form when Haliburton returns.
There's plenty to like about Emanuel Sharp as an off-ball 3&D player and a culture setter. Very hard worker and got a guaranteed contract.
Bub is still playing poorly to close out the season and is teetering on top 300 per-game value. It might be curtains for him soon.
TJ McConnell continues trucking along as a key piece in Indiana as a backup guard. We know what to expect at this point.
With the recent Clippers moves with adding Rui, it feels like DJJ could be one of the odd men out. He's still got some juice, so we'll see what happens.
Wade was a great undrafted gem for the Cavs and plays a steady bench role. Really good IRL player but essentially a cardio guy for fantasy purposes.
Jovic has been downright awful this year. No clue what happened, but good chance he gets salary dumped or used in filler for a trade soon.
The offense remains a work in progress, but if you want to bet on the tools, athleticism, and two-way appeal, Thiero has a lot to love.
Jordan Miller had a nice season with the Clippers. There's sure to be questions in their rotation and how he fits in. I'm not a strong believer.
Duncan Robinson gets a little bit more competition for touches with Isaiah Joe, but he remains the best shooter of the team.
THJ was a 6th Man of the Year Finalist and played a key role for Denver. Expecting him to re-sign here.
Caruso in OKC is making for some terrifying defense. He's a winning player, but spending the remainder of his prime on a deep contender is not A+ for fantasy.
Isaiah Joe was one of OKC's victims for consolidation. He heads to Detroit to bolster their shooting.
LaRavia has impressed on occasion in LA. He's settled into a career as a role player moving forward.
I don't know how he does it, but Andre Drummond continues to survive and deliver some quality play in philly.
Landale has played some decent ball for Atlanta and will likely stick around as a backup/3rd stringer.
Entering the last year of his rookie contract, we still really don't know what Walker is going to be. Good tanking year numbers, but can he show anything this year?
Barlow has played a surprising amount for Philly, starting more games than you'd think. Not a ton of fantasy upside here, at least from recent returns.
AJ Green is one of the bigger losers of the Giannis trade with a ton of guards in the rotation now. He probably needs a trade to return to relevancy.
At 40 years old, Al Horford is somehow still kicking. With Quinten Post gone, there will be hope for him to keep playing at a good level.
This year may be Holmes' last chance at securing a role with Denver. He'll face competition with Marvin Bagley III in the frontcourt.
Ryan Dunn hasn't progressed much besides some 3PT strides, but he remains a bad offensive player and hasn't shown much in the stocks department.
Missi is unfortunately buried in New Orleans given their current big situation with Derik Queen. He'll need a trade to be relevant again.
The Kings salary dumped Devin Carter to the Hawks. There is a chance he can figure it out here as a bench guy.
Somehow, I've forgotten to add Marcus Smart over into multiple updates. He's back now, and has been playing a good role for LA.
Watkins has shown he has some juice to be a good rotation player for Washington. He fits their defensive identity well. He might play more than you think this year.
Diawara has impressed me in his flashes this year. He's on a deep team and minutes may be tough to come by, but I like him as a long-term stash.
Bagley's been playing some decent ball recently in Washington and Dallas. He'll be tasked with backing up Nikola Jokic this year.
JWill probably deserves to be higher than this because he's legitimately solid as a rotation piece, but it's hard to trust he has a role of much size at all.
I still don't know what Cody Williams is supposed to be, but I think the growth we've seen is notable. I'm giving him a chance on a 3rd year breakout despite the drop.
Kornet has shown some stuff for fantasy, but the fact that San Antonio drafted two centers in the first round speaks volumes about his future here.
Caleb Love burst onto the scene early for Portland with some great scoring stretches. Doesn't do much other than chuck up shots.
I'm very skeptical of all this, but Leonard Miller has been showing some real signs of life in Chicago. Will be keeping an eye on this in the offseason.
I don't buy IJax much as an NBA player still. Still, with YKN out indefinitely, he could snag a short-term role.
Following the Ja trade, Krejci is very quietly a winner. The Blazers have lackluster wing/forward depth. Keep an eye here for deep leagues.
Richard has proven to be a notable role player for Golden State. The minutes are always going to be screwy, but maybe there's more of a chance this year.
Grant Williams tore his ACL this past year and is expected to make a full recovery. He's not a priority piece, but he might play more than we think this year.
Goga continues to flash on occasion, but I don't think he'll ever fully put it all together unless some desparate team swipes him up this summer.
There's a very compelling case that Patrick Williams is one of the worst players in the NBA right now.
Goodwin has had some nice moments over the year and continues to look interesting for a deep bench guy.
Mo Wagner returns from his ACL injury to play a backup role in Brooklyn. He'll definitely get some run in the short term.
I'm keeping a close eye on Cisse moving forward. Really intriguing advanced numbers. Could be a great player hiding in plain sight.
McNeeley hasn't popped much yet, but he's shown a little in Charlotte that suggest more could come when he gets a consistent role.
Gradey Dick struggled for Toronto and now gets a clean slate with the Clippers. This is has chance to find a role and salvage his career.
I don't really know why Trajan Langdon gave Kevin Huerter that contract. Hopefully he has a little juice left.
I'm not overwhelmingly confident that Ben Saraf will evolve into a good shooter, or a clearcut NHA player long term, but there is some appeal as a big guard.
Russ went from almost being done as an NBA player to being the starter in Sacramento. It is Sacramento, but he does look revitalized on a bad team like this.
With a lot of questions about centers in Detroit, there is a real chance Ugonna Oyenso takes up a solid role as a backup.
Karlo has some interesting appeal as a floor spacer that can block shots. There's just a lot of big men in New Orleans and his opportunities are not all there.
Ron Harper Jr. has had some nice flashes for Boston. I'm not sure if he's much of a long-term NBA player but I'm keeping an eye on him.
Adams was badly missed this season and in the playoffs during Sengun's lowlights. He'll maintain a key role when healthy for '26-'27.
Powell still has a lot of potential as a 3&D wing with Brooklyn, but he hasn't showed much to date.
In theory, Braden Smith is a perfect fit for Indiana and could find something here. The issue is that Indiana's guard depth is completely full.
Brown has not been as good as I'd hoped returning to Denver, but he's at least playing a role again and might earn more burn as the year goes on.
I still believe there could be something there for Brandon Williams despite finishing below the top 250 in 9Cat on the year.
Brook Lopez is almost done in the NBA, but he's still got some juice and will play a decent chunk of minutes with YKN still recovering from his Lisfranc injury.
Ellis was very disappointing this past year in Sacramento and Cleveland. We'll see what kind of year he has for Brooklyn.
Middleton is reaching the end of his career and was dumped to Dallas in the AD trade. He re-signed in Washington to keep mentoring their youngsters.
KCP is likely to be bought out or make some agreement with MEM to find a new team. Could he return to being a decent role player?
Edwards could see a bump during the season with the 76ers' lackluster depth. He's occasionally shown flashes but I don't see a consistent role player here.
Strawther's fantasy game is pretty weak, but he can shoot and could see marginal opportunities if Peyton Watson goes elsewhere.
DFS lives! He was in a rough situation with injuries and a contract that aged like milk immediately. Could he bounce back this year in Charlotte?
Hawkins is mostly just a 3PT specialist and nothing more. He's mainly just a rotation piece at this point.
Okoro is what he is at this stage in his career. Chicago will use him some but don't expect anything for fantasy.
It wasn't long ago that Bogdan was still a good player. Could he return to form here in Houston?
Barnes still has some juice even in San Antonio. We know what he is as a boring forward who can pop on occasion.
As always with Luka Garza, he's got some juice on offense, but he continues to have issues on defense that make him a liability.
Kevon Looney is seemingly pretty washed after last year in New Orleans. Not loving him as the primary backup at center if the Knicks lose MitchRob.
Furphy tore his ACL in late February. There is still some upside here but missing much-needed development time is going to hurt.
Bones Hyland revived his career with Minnesota after nearly falling out of the NBA. The team feels a bit too deep at guard for him to make much sense.
Tarik has been long rumored to want to make the NBA jump, and here he comes on a two-year deal in Dallas. 3PT shooting is the name of the game.
As usual, Vukcevic continues to tease good fantasy play here and there. He may not ever be a full-time NBA player.
Sochan was waived by San Antonio and picked up by New York. He'll have to hope someone takes a cheap flier on him this summer, but it's not looking good.
In the Pantheon of quirked up white boys, Kolek is decently up there in the NBA section. To date though, he's yet to earn a consistent role with the Knicks.
Despite playing on lesser minutes, Clark is a legitimately great defender. Could he secure a bigger role this next year?
Amari Williams has some real potential here in Boston with MitchRob's injury issues. Good passer, could be a serious diamond in the rough.
CPJ is actually one of the more interesting role players out there that could be a hit if Cleveland's bench wasn't so deep. Worth a watch to see what happens.
Caris LeVert has been awful for a while and I'm guessing his NBA career is nearing its end after his current contract.
Proctor is waiting behind Craig Porter Jr. for NBA minutes. Likely won't happen for him this year unless there's injuries.
Shamet signed a deal to return to the Knicks. He stepped up this year to play a decent role.
I was kind of out on Sasser before the Dallas trade. Now? I might be a liiiittle moved and will be watching this.
Achiuwa is struggling to make it in the NBA. He's currently with Sacramento but already bounced around multiple teams this season.
Thomas found his way out of the NBA pretty quickly after being waived by Brooklyn. Get ready to learn Chinese, buddy.
With the Heat's lack of depth, Fontecchio has a little something to tap into off the bench.
Hayes and Walker Kessler basically swap spots. Hayes will be a backup big to Jusuf Nurkic. I'm hoping there's another trade coming here.
The Heat always manage to find one of these guys who breaks the undrafted mold. Is Myron Gardner one? He's had some OK moments.
Corey Kispert is running out of time as an NBA player and I don't see much of a relevant role for him in Atlanta moving forward.
The hope is that Gary Trent Jr. ends up on a decent team that gives him a one-year flier. He might be about done in the NBA.
Plowden showed some real stuff for Sacramento, and I don't think it was just Silly Season stuff.
There is a chance Josh Green could play a meaningful role in Minnesota if there's injuries to their other wings, but he's essentially just a cardio guy with little to offer.
There is a strong possibility that JV is leaving the NBA this or next year. If he stays, he remains a deep league hold for contenders as Jokic's backup.
Spencer Jones is an innings eater (complimentary) and his fantasy output has been inconsistent, but he's playing a nice amount of minutes. Continuing to monitor him.
Vanderbilt is a way better IRL player than fantasy, and even then, he's not doing much on either front.
Gueye has been a nerd favorite in years' past, but I don't see much for him moving forward unless he takes a jump or is traded.
Charlotte has found a potential multi-year role player in Sion James. He's mostly an empty calories/innings eater type.
Jamal Cain was genuinely very good for Orlando in the playoffs and has bought himself a few more years in the NBA as an energy guy.
Broome was a brutal pick for Philly. Didn't like it at the time, makes it even worse as the 4th big behind Embiid, Bona and Hukporti.
Mann is one of the quintessential master of none who can do a couple things OK. Not much to say about him.
Zach Collins got himself another payday in Chicago, to my surprise. He'll be the third big behind Nic Claxton and Jalen Smith.
Clarkson played a role for New York this year and got rewarded with a multi-year contract.
Klay's time in the NBA is nearing its end after a career-worst year. He's just 74 away from overtaking Ray Allen with the 3rd most 3's all-time.
I love Spencer's landing spot in Phoenix, but can he get some run here with how deep their guard room is?
Koby Brea might be a role player that can't do a ton offensively, but he more than makes up for it as a pure 3PT specialist who's shot 43.4% from 3 in his CBB career.
Rocco needs a ton of time to keep developing, but early G League returns have been pretty good so far. I just don't know if he's ever a full-time NBA player.
Jericho Sims is buried in Milwaukee and their weird depth chart. Don't see him ever being relevant again.
He's baaaack. Bassey heads to Golden State where he could potentially snatch a role as a third big.
Hukporti heads to Philly to be the third big behind Joel Embiid and Adem Bona. He'll get some burn if Embiid gets hurt.
DLo is on what might be his last chance to keep the career and name recognition standing. He's been dumped to two different teams so far in 2026.
Ziaire's time in Brooklyn is coming to an end. The hope is someone desperate like the Lakers give him a shot and he finds a role, but I'm not sure it happens.
Bouyea is locked into the Suns for this next season. Phoenix has a lot of depth, but is there a possible Bouyea breakout here?
We know what it is with GP2 at this point. Solid IRL rotation guy but he can't do much of anything for fantasy aside from the steals.
After the whole Jaden Ivey debacle, the important thing is that he's healthy physically and mentally. A journey back into the NBA is possible.
Knecht is arguably one of the worst players in the NBA and his career might be close to over at 25 (his second season).
Prince got traded to Detroit to clear up roster space in Milwaukee. Real chance he plays an actual, albeit small, role.
Kenny Hustle returns to OKC with the good vibes. End-of-bench guy at this point, but he's still got some juice.
Vince has had a tough run recently with the trade to Utah, tearing his ACL and getting waived. I'm still hopeful for him breaking back in when healthy.
Rupert showed some legit flashes at a lot of points in his career. Him and Caleb Love had good synergy in Portland. Could he be something here in Philly?
Tomlin really impressed me at Summer League and is starting to break into CLE's rotation a bit. Keep an eye on him.
Peavy has some good role player stuff despite being a poor shooter/offensive player to date. Could be something to watch in deep leagues.
Not much to say here about Dru Smith. Can't shoot, can defend. Don't know how he fits into the equation in Miami.
I think it's telling that Indiana was ready to move on from Kam Jones so fast. Milwaukee could be an interesting spot for him.
Martin is smaller and lacks a clear high-end NBA skill to make up for size, but his energy and pure athleticism is solid. He got himself a guaranteed deal this summer.
If you want to hold out any hope for another second team opportunity guy, maybe Jett Howard can be one. He's struggled to do anything for Orlando.
Caleb Martin has barely played and been bad when he has for Dallas. Another masterful gambit, Nico Harrison.
Old Man Conley's still kicking, long after the NBA has moved on from his archetype. He ends up in Boston for (probably) one last ride.
An interesting move for Utah as Okogie heads out to SLC with a 2-year deal in hand. Good defender. Could we see him get any run?
Buddy is mega washed at this point. He shot poorly last season and looks like he has no chance to be anything but salary trade filler in ATL.
We know who Matisse Thybulle as a defender. Remains to be seen if a contender picks him up.
Julian Reese has been a Silly Season hero with how he's played for Washington. Could he end up as a longer term deep bench guy?
Watford has been a bench piece with occasional flashes this year. Nothing crazy but can pop off and has some good passing to his game.
Lanier is a pretty meh fantasy player for me. Mostly will just be shooting 3s and not much else. He'll be a better IRL player than a fantasy player.
The guard room in Houston got pretty deep, but Aaron Holiday has managed to hang around for a bit.
Bronny's shown some occasional NBA stuff, but I don't see much for him. Guessing he's traded wherever LeBron goes.
I think Brooks Barnhizer has shown some good fantasy appeal. I don't think he's got a big chance of being a full-time NBA player but there is something here.
Mashack is stuck and buried deep in Memphis. He definitely seems like he could be a legit NBA player.
Nick Richards has flashed at different spots over the year. I think he's worth a spin on a one-year minimum.
Jaden Hardy got sent to LA in the DeAndre Ayton. Before anyone asks: No, I don't think this is a diamond in the rough for the Lakers.
I was shocked to find out that Elijah Harkless left Utah and signed a two-way deal with Detroit. He's a sleeper to watch.
Unfortunately, aura can't save your career. Tre Mann's full-time NBA career is pretty much done.
SloMo heads to Toronto as an end-of-bench piece. Not a ton left in the tank these days.
I hate giving up on players we've just barely seen play, but AJ Johnson is unlikely to ever be a full-time NBA player. He still has so much rawness to his game.
Green has played a small role for Detroit almost all year and looked OK doing so. Almost no upside here.
Ben Sheppard has showed some stuff here and there for Indiana. Unfortunately, I don't think he's much more than an end-of-bench guy.
Whitmore fell out of favor in Washington this past year and was diagnosed with DVT. He'll have one last year to prove himself as an NBA player.
I had hopes for Jonathan Mogbo finding a role in the NBA despite being a funky fitting player. I don't see him being a full-time NBA player again.
Ochai isn't anything special on the court, but we might see him get a one-year minimum and contribute something. Might just be an end-of-bench or G Leaguer.
Jackson has flashed plenty for Indiana over the years. Unfortunately, they're so deep at guard that Jackson is unlikely to ever get his fair shot here.
We know what it is with Thomas Bryant. Dude is not very good, but as a third big, sure, I guess.
Pacome Dadiet has yet to show anything yet for the Knicks. The hope is he can be traded and show some signs of life.
Nance heads to Indiana as just a likely locker room guy. Always wondering if he's got any of his vintage game left.
Svi has flashed pretty often for Utah in his time there, but with Utah gearing up in a big way, I don't see him playing much for them again.
Jonathan Isaac was waived and subsequently picked back up in Orlando on a cheap deal. Don't think there's much here.
Toohey had a bad start to his NBA career following an ACL tear, but I still have hope he can be an NBA player.
OMax flashed some stuff this past season during Silly Season. Not sure he's ever going to be a full-time NBA guy.
Murray was just in the Ja Morant trade to make the money work. I don't expect him to play much here (if at all).
Jalen Wilson will be looking for a new team this summer after Brooklyn declined his QO.
Lonzo Ball might be done as an NBA player, unfortunately. He has a case for one of the worst players in the NBA playing real minutes last year.
TJD has fallen off the map this past year and barely played for either of Toronto or Golden State. Does he still have a shot to be an NBA player?
Taelon Peter hasn't shown much yet for the Pacers after snagging him in the late 2nd round in 2025. His shooting could get him some looks still.
It remains to be seen if and when Nunez ever comes over. He has had some concerning knee injuries that I'm keeping an eye on.
Clint Capela is mostly just an end-of-bench player at this point (which is wild to say). Not likely to be much in the NBA again.
